reasoning: Both meetings are firmly within the same tightening regime: the June meeting held rates at 5–5.25% with a skip while explicitly retaining a tightening bias, and the July meeting delivered the anticipated 25bp hike to 5.25–5.5% — a continuation of the established cycle, not a regime transition. The reaction function (data-dependent tightening to return inflation to 2%), dominant tool (rate hikes + QT), and trajectory (tightening) are unchanged. Market participants widely expected this hike and most viewed it as potentially the last of the cycle, but the Committee itself retained identical forward-guidance language about 'additional policy firming that may be appropriate,' signaling no strategic reorientation.
key_quote: In determining the extent of additional policy firming that may be appropriate to return inflation to 2 percent over time, the Committee will take into account the cumulative tightening of monetary policy, the lags with which monetary policy affects economic activity and inflation, and economic and financial developments.
